properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony asked for it to be thought through this way rather than built on the spot, 2026-08-21: "I'd like to capture as the third leg... maybe we brainstorm on it and test out our new concept to see if it links to other related ideas? then we accept the proposed idea and then implement?"

THE OPEN QUESTION: what, if anything, should notice an idea that connects to nothing?

WHY IT IS OPEN AT ALL. The brainstorm skill now asks for the honest edges AND for a written line when none is drawn. That is the INSTRUCTION leg. `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` says an instruction without a detector leaves the vocabulary empty in EVERY project, not just this one — and the 145-ideas-12-edges measurement is what that emptiness looks like when only two legs are present. So the missing leg is named and the shape of the hole is known.

🛑🛑 AND THE OBVIOUS BUILD COLLIDES WITH THE SKILL IT WOULD SERVE. brainstorm/SKILL.md step 2 says, in as many words: "Do not run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes. It would ask the user to firm up exactly what they deliberately left soft, which teaches them that thinking out loud has a cost." A detector that fires on every unlinked idea is precisely that. Built naively, the third leg would tax the one activity the whole skill exists to keep free.

⭐ THE COLLISION WAS ALREADY SETTLED, ELEVEN DAYS EARLY, BY A REQUIREMENT NEITHER NODE MENTIONS. `req:detecting-is-not-asking` (Anthony, 2026-08-19): detecting a gap and inviting its closure are DIFFERENT ACTS and only one is urgent — detection stays unconditional, the invitation waits for a boundary. Every option below is really a position on WHERE this one lands on that line. That is the finding of this brainstorm, and it came out of the search the new linking step spends rather than from thinking harder.

=== THE OPTIONS ===

(a) A `detect_gaps` finding — say `unlinked_idea` — on any proposed Decision with no relation edge and no "no real relation" line. CHEAP: the detector framework exists and this is a two-predicate rule. EXPENSIVE: it lands in the list a user reads as their to-do, which is the nudge the skill forbids, and it would land there 111 times on this graph the day it shipped. A finding that fires a hundred times on day one teaches people to filter the whole category.

(b) The same rule, but the INVITATION held until a boundary — a capture-session, an increment close — while the detection itself runs always. Exactly the shape `req:detecting-is-not-asking` describes, and it keeps thinking-out-loud free at the moment of thinking. More work than (a): the detector is the easy half, the boundary is the part that has to be chosen and honoured.

(c) Not a per-node finding at all, but a POPULATION LINE in the sweep's coverage — "145 ideas, 12 linked, 111 reaching nothing" — reported as a number, never as a defect against any one idea. CHEAPEST and quietest, and it inherits the property the coverage work was built for: a detector that reports zero because it had NOTHING TO RUN ON is distinguishable from one that ran clean. It answers "is the linking step working" without ever telling any individual idea it is deficient. WEAKEST on the three legs, though: a number in a report is not something the loop asks about, and the leg was specified as a detector that surfaces absence.

(d) Nothing on the ideas; the compliance check on the SKILL is the whole third leg. Already built as `LINK_CONTRACT` in skill_lint (2026-08-21). HONEST LIMIT, stated plainly: that check guards the INSTRUCTION against deletion, not the graph against being unlinked. It would pass green over a graph where no agent ever drew an edge. It is a real guard, but it is not this leg.

(e) Do nothing and let the instruction carry it. The null option, and it deserves a fair hearing: it is exactly what was in force for the previous 145 ideas, and it is what produced 12 edges. The evidence against it is unusually direct.

=== WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN ===
Whether the "no real relation" line can be READ mechanically at all. The skill asks for it in prose, and a detector that cannot tell "somebody looked and found nothing" from "nobody looked" would report the two identically — which is the exact failure the line was added to prevent. If it cannot be read, the line needs a structural home (a property, or an edge to nothing) before any of (a)-(c) can distinguish them. THAT QUESTION IS PRIOR TO THE CHOICE, and it is measurable rather than arguable.

=== HOW THIS NODE WAS LINKED ===
Recorded here because it is the first use of the step it is about. The near-matches came from four searches run before writing; four edges were drawn and each names its reason in `evidence`. The collision in the second paragraph and the reconciliation in the third were both found in those hits, not reasoned out — which is the case the linking step was arguing for.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ ACCEPTED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-21 — OPTION (b), WITH THE PRIOR QUESTION ANSWERED FIRST
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

HIS CHOICE: detect always, invite at a boundary. The detector runs unconditionally so the record stays honest; the INVITATION waits for a boundary (a capture-session, an increment close) so that thinking out loud costs nothing at the moment of thinking. This is `req:detecting-is-not-asking` applied to the case it was not written for, and it is why the collision recorded above does not have to be paid for.

AND THE PREREQUISITE IS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE, not a caveat on it. "Looked and found nothing" needs a home a detector can READ. The skill asks for it in prose today, and prose cannot be told apart from silence — so the very first thing built has to be a structural place for that judgement, on the pattern `distinct_from` already uses on the dedup guard: the guard does not infer that you considered the duplicate, it makes you say so, and then the saying is a fact rather than an inference.

WITHOUT IT THE DETECTOR WOULD REPORT THE TWO STATES IDENTICALLY — an idea somebody looked at and found genuinely new, and an idea nobody has opened — which is the exact failure the "no real relation" line was added to prevent. A detector that cannot tell those apart is not a weaker version of this leg. It is a machine for producing false findings about people who did the work.

⭐ SO THE THREE STATES THE BUILD MUST DISTINGUISH ARE:
  (A) LINKED — carries at least one relation to another node.
  (B) REVIEWED AND DELIBERATELY UNLINKED — somebody judged the near-matches and drew nothing, and said so.
  (C) NOBODY LOOKED — the only one of the three that is a finding.

Option (c)'s population line is not a rival to this and should not be argued against it: a count over the whole graph answers "is the linking step working at all", which is a different question from "which idea has nobody opened". If it is cheap once (C) is computable, it is worth having beside it.
properties.name: OPEN — what should notice an idea that connects to nothing?
